tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

contextLabel.description: Short header tying the suggestion to the user request.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

keywords.description: Topic keywords from the user's request.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c__batch
tools.description: Create a doc, or apply several operations to one doc atomically.

tools.name: mcp__1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c__guide
tools.description: Docs guides: topic.instructions repeats the server instructions. Read it only if your client dropped them. Also topic.<name>, refusal.<code>. After a doc's birth → ["topic.index"].

items.description: topic.<name> (instructions, index, editing, tabs, comments, charts, chart-definition, diagram, uploads, sharing, skill) or refusal.<code>; several per call is fine.

tools.name: mcp__1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c__update
tools.description: Edit a tab's contents, rename a doc or tab, or change a stored value.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_pr__bind_pr
tools.description: Bind this session to a PR the PR bar did not pick up (fork remote, GitHub Enterprise host, PR opened elsewhere) by its URL. The repository must be this checkout's origin or one the user's sessions already have a PR bound from. Restores a dismissed open PR. The user is asked to approve (in auto mode the app may approve without asking, judging from the conversation, except to restore a PR the user dismissed; in bypass permissions mode it does not ask), so bind only a PR the user asked you to track.

url.description: The pull request URL, e.g. https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123.

_consent.description: Set by the app. Do not set it.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_pr__get_status
tools.description: Read the pull request bound to a Code session in this app (default "self") and its CI monitor: PR number/url/state/branches, CI check counts and failing check names, review decision, mergeability, and the auto_fix / auto_merge / auto_archive_on_close switches. Served from the app's cache. Use after `gh pr create` instead of polling `gh pr checks`.

session_id.description: The session to read: the literal string "self" (default) or a sessionId from ccd_session_mgmt list_sessions.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_pr__set_monitor
tools.description: Set this session's CI monitor switches for its bound, open PR. auto_fix: the app wakes this session with a `<ci-monitor-event>` on CI failures, merge conflicts and review comments; turn it on only for a PR this session opened. address_comments must equal auto_fix on this machine. auto_archive_on_close: archive this session once the PR merges or closes. Pass only the switches to change, and the PR's url with auto_fix. The user is asked to approve each call (in auto mode the app may approve without asking, and in bypass permissions mode it does not ask), so only call it when the user asked for that switch.

auto_fix.description: Wake this session on CI failures, merge conflicts and review comments.

address_comments.description: Review-comment delivery. On this machine it is the same switch as auto_fix and must equal it when passed.

auto_archive_on_close.description: Archive this session once its PR merges or closes.

url.description: The bound pull request's URL, as get_status reports it. Required with auto_fix.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

Call this when it went stale: the work was done here after all (by you or the user), it turned out unnecessary, or you proposed a better-scoped replacement (propose the new one first, then dismiss the old task_id). A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

task_id.description: The task_id the start_session proposal returned.

reason.description: Optional one-line reason the suggestion is no longer needed, e.g. "fixed in this session" or "superseded by task_ab12cd34".

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session
tools.description: Move the task you are in the middle of into its own session (a fork of this conversation plus your remaining plan) so you can answer the user now. Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task being moved.

remaining_plan.description: What is left to do: steps, files, what done looks like.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

title.description: Short noun-phrase title for the chapter (under 40 chars). Shown in the table of contents.

summary.description: Optional one-line summary of what this chapter covers. Shown on hover in the table of contents.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__read_widget_context
tools.description: Read context from an embedded interactive widget. Widgets are rendered alongside chat from prior tool calls and can be interacted with by the user. Call this when you need to know the current state of a widget.

tool_name.description: The name of the widget tool to get context for

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__ccd_view__show_pane
tools.description:
Show one of this session's side panes in the user's view of the Claude desktop app, beside the conversation.

Panes: "diff" (the session's changes; optional `path` scrolls to that file, `diff_scope` picks all branch changes, uncommitted changes only, or one commit), "file" (`path` opens that file in the Files pane at `line`; must be inside the session's working directory or a folder the user granted), "terminal" (optional `tab_id` switches to that open tab), "pr" (the session's pull request), "tasks" (background tasks), "plan", "preview" (the Browser pane, once this session has a page open in it), "artifact" (the artifacts this session published). A page in a hidden Browser pane runs as a background page: animation may not run at all, and on some systems timers slow down once you haven't touched the page for a while. Showing the pane with that page's tab in front helps only while the Claude window is itself in view (not minimized or covered by another app), so don't rely on timing or performance numbers from the page unless the user is watching it.

Prefer showing over describing: after finishing a set of edits, show the diff; when pointing the user at code, open the file at the line. It only changes what is on screen for this session — if the session isn't open in any window it does nothing and says so (tell the user what to look at instead), and it never takes focus from another session. A pane in a window of its own is left where it is, never raised, reopened here or changed, and the result says so: tell the user to look there.

path.description: For "file": the file to open (absolute, or relative to the working directory). For "diff": the changed file to scroll to.

diff_scope.description: For "diff": "all" (branch changes, the default), "uncommitted", or a commit SHA.

tab_id.description: For "terminal": the open tab to switch to, by the tab_id a terminal tool or an attached terminal snippet gave you. Omit to show the terminal as it is.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__find
tools.description: Search the current page in the Browser pane for elements whose accessibility-tree line (role / name / text) contains `query`, case-insensitively. Returns up to 20 `ref_N` matches usable with `computer`/`form_input`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

query.description: Text to look for in an element's role, name or text (case-insensitive substring, e.g. "Sign in", "search", "Add to cart").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__form_input
tools.description: Set the value of a form element identified by `ref` (from read_page/find). Handles input/textarea/select/checkbox/contenteditable.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract the visible text of the Browser pane's page (article/main content first, falls back to body innerText).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__javascript_tool
tools.description: Execute JavaScript in the Browser pane's page for DEBUGGING and INSPECTION only. Do NOT use this to implement UI changes — edit source code instead.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description: Action to perform (only `javascript_exec` is supported).

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. Return values are serialized as JSON.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__navigate
tools.description: Navigate the Browser pane to a URL, or go "back"/"forward" in history. If the Browser pane isn't open yet, this opens it at the URL (no dev server needed).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

force.description: If the page shows a "Leave site?" dialog because of unsaved changes, discard those changes and navigate anyway. Defaults to false.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_list
tools.description: List servers started with preview_start. Returns serverIds for use with other preview_* tools.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_logs
tools.description: Get server stdout/stderr output. Use to check for build errors, verify server behavior, or read debug output. Use 'level' to filter to errors only, or 'search' to filter for specific text. Use after preview_start.

level.description: Filter by level: 'all' (default) shows all output, 'error' shows only lines containing error/exception/failed/fatal

search.description: Filter to lines containing this text (e.g., '[DEBUG]', 'POST /api')

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_start

name.description: Server name from .claude/launch.json.

url.description: URL to open in the Browser pane without a dev server (instead of starting one by `name`).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_stop
tools.description: Stop a server started with preview_start.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_console_messages
tools.description: Get console output (log, info, warn, error, debug) from the Browser pane.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

limit.description: Max entries to return (default: 50, max: 200).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_network_requests
tools.description: List network requests, or fetch a specific response body by `requestId`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

urlPattern.description: Substring filter on the request URL as listed (auth values show as REDACTED).

requestId.description: If provided, returns the response body for this request instead of listing.

limit.description: Max entries to return when listing (default: 50).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_page
tools.description: Read the current page in the Browser pane as a YAML-style accessibility tree. Each interactive element is tagged `[ref_N]` for use with `computer`/`form_input`/`find`. Prefer this over screenshot for verifying text and structure. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default; if it exceeds the limit it is truncated with a note — pass a larger max_chars, or use ref_id/depth to focus.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

filter.description: 'interactive' returns only clickable/typable elements; 'all' (default) returns the full tree.

ref_id.description: Restrict the tree to descendants of this `ref_N` (from a previous read_page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_close
tools.description: Close one Browser pane tab. Closing the last tab closes the Browser pane itself (reopen it with `preview_start`).

tabId.description: Tab to close.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_context
tools.description: List every Browser pane tab (origin only — titles are page-authored). Returns {browserOpen, tabs: [{tabId, origin, isActive}]} plus a line saying whether the pane is currently displayed or hidden (a hidden pane still works, but its page runs as a background page, so timing and performance numbers from it can be off; prefer `read_page` / `get_page_text` over screenshots while it is hidden). browserOpen is false (and tabs empty) until `preview_start` or `navigate` opens the pane, so you don't need to call this before opening it.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_create
tools.description: Open a fresh blank Browser pane tab; returns the new tabId. Opens in the background by default — set `foreground: true` when the user wants to watch. Prefer `preview_start` with a `url` when you know the destination; use `navigate` to load a URL into a blank tab.

foreground.description: Front the new tab (user asked to see it or is following along). Default false: open behind the user's current tab.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_select
tools.description: Front the given Browser pane tab. Background tabs keep running while you drive them, so front one only when the user should look — or for a page that pauses itself while hidden (e.g. a video player).

tabId.description: Tab to front.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
tools.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. content.text:
## Critical review

**1. Nothing separates one section from the next.** I measured the page. All 15 sections below the hero have no background of their own, the same 56px top padding, and the same pattern: a small mono label, a left-aligned 31–36px heading and a paragraph. Your eye never gets a "new chapter" cue, so it reads as one long document.

Apple does the opposite. Every message sits on its own tile, which is a solid surface alternating black and light grey (`#f5f5f7`). Each tile is about 692px tall, with a 12px white gap between tiles, and that gap is the separator. Below the big tiles comes a two-up grid of smaller tiles with the same 12px gap.

**2. Fifteen sections and no story.** The order doesn't build an argument:
- The podcast ("Watch and listen") is 5th, before you've shown what Maester checks.
- The Zero Trust Assessment appears in the hero, the screenshot tabs, Coverage, its own section and Packs.
- Packs are split across the growth section, the ZTA section and the Packs section, while "Write your own" sits apart from them.
- The Maester Cloud upsell sits between Sponsors and Community.

A visitor can't tell what the page wants them to do.

**3. The headings are all the same size.** The page title is 61px and every section heading is 31–36px, left-aligned and in the same style. Apple makes each tile's heading the biggest thing on it (56px on the full-width tiles, 40px on the half tiles), centred, with one line beneath it and two buttons at most.

**4. The same facts repeat.** "890 checks" is in the hero, the stats band and the growth section, and the ZTA story is told three times. Every repeat makes the page longer and weakens each section.

**5. The calls to action don't match.** Some sections end in a button, some in a text link, some in a code block and some in nothing.

## Plan

**One tile component, three tones.** Add a `HomeSection.astro` with a `tone` setting: white, grey or ink (dark). It would give every section:
- full width, or a rounded tile with 12px gaps between tiles
- a centred header: label, a 48–56px heading, one sentence underneath, and at most two buttons
- a minimum height, so every chapter feels like a screen of its own

Dark mode gets matching versions of each tone.

**Cut 15 sections down to 8 chapters**, alternating tones so each boundary is visible:

| # | Chapter | Built from | Tone |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | What Maester is | Hero + report screenshot | white |
| 2 | Proof | Stats band | grey strip |
| 3 | The checks | Growth chart + Coverage (frameworks) | ink |
| 4 | How it works | Video + Automate (run it every day) | grey |
| 5 | Extend it | ZTA + Packs + Write your own, as three half-width tiles | white |
| 6 | 3.0 | What's new, as one short tile linking to the launch post | ink |
| 7 | Community | Contributors + podcast + sponsors | grey |
| 8 | Next step | Maester Cloud as the closing band | ink |

**Trim the copy.** Give each fact one home: the check count lives in chapter 3 and ZTA in chapter 5. Each tile carries one heading, one sentence and its buttons, and the detail moves to the linked pages.

**Use one button style everywhere:** a solid button for the main action and a text link for the second.

**Check the result** at desktop, tablet and phone widths, in light and dark mode, and make sure nothing still blends into its neighbour.

I'd keep this separate from [maester365/maester#2728](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2728), on its own branch built on top of it, since it reuses the growth section.

Maester
What it isThe checksHow it worksExtend3.0Community
Get started

Open source · MIT · Free forever

Test your Microsoft 365 security every day.

One PowerShell run checks Entra, Azure, Exchange, Teams and Active Directory, and writes a report you can act on.

PS>Install-Module Maester -AllowPrerelease
QuickstartSee a live report

Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux · Nothing leaves your tenant

OverviewAction planA findingFrameworksMITRE ATT&CKZero Trust
1,254Checks run
912Passed
187Failed
155Skipped, with a reason
MT.1054Phishing-resistant MFA is required for admins
CIS 5.1.5.1Users can't consent to apps
ZTA 21780Legacy authentication is blocked
625K+PowerShell Gallery downloads
1,872Checks
1.2KGitHub stars
74+Contributors

01The checks

1,872 checks. Every framework your auditors ask about.

Each check names the requirement it implements, so one report answers CIS, CISA, Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment, MITRE ATT&CK and NIST at once.

Browse the checksHow checks map to frameworks
149 CIS Microsoft 36576 CISA SCuBA364 Zero Trust AssessmentEIDSCAORCAMITRE ATT&CKNIST SP 800-53

Checks by release

Built in · 890Shipped packs · 364Community packs · 618

Checks by product

Entra ID468
Active Directory275
Defender151
Intune140
Exchange122
Azure94
Teams57

02How it works

From install to a report in five minutes.

Then run it every night from the pipeline you already have.

Watch the 1:40 tourRead the quickstart
▶
1InstallInstall-Module Maester
2ConnectConnect-Maester
3RunInvoke-Maester
4Automatemaester-action@main

Runs in GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, Azure Automation, Container Apps, GitLab, Bitbucket and Terraform, and sends results to email, Teams and Slack.

03Maester Packs

Need a check Maester doesn't have? Add a pack.

Packs add checks from Microsoft and the community, in the same report.

Browse packsHow packs work
Ships with Maester · 364 checksMicrosoft Zero Trust Assessment

Microsoft's assessment, run from Maester, every result beside Maester's own checks.

Community · 5 checksLeast Privileged MSGraph

Service principals hold only the Graph permissions they actually use.

Community · 8 checksRKSolutions Intune Anomalies

Devices that miss protection, drift or fall out of management.

Write your own

Write your policies as tests.

One PowerShell function. Maester runs it with everything else.

Write your first testTest builder
function Test-CT1001 {
  [MaesterTest(Id = 'CT.1001',
    Title = 'Only admins can invite guests')]
  param()
  $p = Invoke-MtGraphRequest 'policies/authorizationPolicy'
  $p.allowInvitesFrom -in 'adminsAndGuestInviters'
}

Zero Trust Assessment

Microsoft's assessment, in your Maester report.

The pack ships with Maester. One command runs both.

How the pack works
Invoke-Maester -Pack ZTA

  ✓ 1,254 checks · 364 from Zero Trust
  Report: ./test-results/index.html

04New in 3.0

Maester 3.0. Rebuilt to run faster and say more.

A test engine of its own, checks that ship in the module, and a reason for every skip.

Read the launch postUpgrade from 2.x
Its own engine

Faster, with time-outs, and one row per policy or mailbox.

Pick what to run

By product, framework, severity or ID. Preview with -DryRun.

A reason for every skip

Missing licence, permission or connection, named.

05Community

Built in the open by 74+ contributors.

Security practitioners, Microsoft MVPs and Microsoft engineers write the checks.

Join the DiscordMeet the contributors

Listen

Maester on Entra.Chat

How Xbox secures 70+ Entra tenants every night, and three more episodes.

All episodes

Maester 3.0, and its future, are possible because of you. Help us sustain and improve Maester for the community.

Add a check or write a pack.

Read the manifesto

Every tenant, every run, in one place.

+

One PowerShell run checks Entra, Azure, Exchange, Teams and Active Directory, and writes a report you can act on.

+
QuickstartSee a live report

+

Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux · Nothing leaves your tenant

ZTA 21780Legacy authentication is blocked

+

1,872 checks. Every framework your auditors ask about.

+

Each check names the requirement it implements, so one report answers CIS, CISA, Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment, MITRE ATT&CK and NIST at once.

content.text:
The mock is open in the browser pane at http://localhost:3200/home-mock.html. Use the **Theme** button in the header to switch between light and dark.

**What changed from today's page:**
- **Every section has its own background.** Sections alternate between white, light grey and near-black, with a 12px gap between them, so you can always see where one ends and the next begins. In dark mode the near-black sections take a dark red tint so they still stand apart from the black page.
- **Every section is laid out the same way:** a small label, a large centred heading, one sentence, then one red button and one text link.
- **A chapter bar in the header** (What it is · The checks · How it works · Extend · 3.0 · Community) highlights the chapter you're in as you scroll, so the page's structure is visible at a glance.
- **The 15 sections are now 8:**
  1. The hero, with the report preview.
  2. The stats strip.
  3. **The checks**: the growth chart and checks by product, with the frameworks as chips.
  4. **How it works**: the video, the four steps, and the places it runs.
  5. **Extend**: a wide Packs tile, plus two half-width tiles for "Write your own" and Zero Trust.
  6. **3.0**: three short points and a link to the launch post.
  7. **Community**: the podcast, sponsors and contributing.
  8. **Maester Cloud** as the closing section.
- **Each fact appears once.** The check count lives in "The checks", and the Zero Trust story in "Extend".

I checked it at desktop and phone widths, in both themes, and nothing overflows sideways.

**Caveats:**
- The copy and numbers come from the current page, but the report preview, video, avatars and sponsor logos are placeholders.
- The mock file is in `website/public/` only so the dev server can show it. It isn't committed and shouldn't be. A copy is also at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill--claude-spares-spare-qE5EWv/9948f473-294e-4c13-b6e3-fb178c50639e/scratchpad/home-mock.html`.

import re,sys,collections
s=open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf8').read()
links=re.findall(r'\[([^\]\[]{1,80})\]\((https?://[^)\s]{0,200})',s)
kinds=collections.defaultdict(set)
for text,url in links:
    k='user' if re.search(r'User(Profile|Details)|/users/|userId',url,re.I) else ('group' if 'Group' in url else 'other')
    kinds[k].add(text)
for k,v in kinds.items(): print(k,len(v)); print(sorted(v)[:200] if k=='user' else sorted(v)[:40])
EOF

content.text:
The new homepage and the live demo are working on the local site (http://localhost:3200, open in the browser pane). Microsoft's own Zero Trust report, the one with the Sankey chart, isn't in the demo yet: my build that included it was blocked (details below). I checked the page at desktop and phone widths and in both themes, and the site builds without errors. Nothing is committed; the work is on a new branch, `feat/website-home-chapters`, made from main.

**Homepage**
- The page now follows the mock: eight chapters on alternating white, grey and dark tiles with gaps between them. Each has a centred heading, one sentence, and a red button plus a text link.
- A chapter bar under the site header highlights the chapter you're in as you scroll.

**Live demo**
- The report preview at the top has a new **Live demo** tab. It loads the real report with the Contoso sample data, and visitors can click through all of it.
- **Try the live demo** in the hero opens that tab. **See the plan**, in the Zero Trust tile, opens the demo straight at the Zero Trust plan.
- Two new buttons sit at the right of the tab bar: **full screen** and **open in a new tab**. Full screen works for the still views and the live demo alike. If a browser refuses full screen (iPhone Safari), the button opens the report in a new tab instead.
- The automatic slideshow cycles through the still views only and never switches to the live demo by itself.
- I couldn't test full screen with a real click: clicks in the preview pane don't reach the button. Calling the button directly runs the right code: it asks for full screen and, when that's refused, opens the report in a new tab.

**New report views**
- I recaptured all the views, so they now show the blade layout, where the sidebar folds to icons and a pack's or framework's own menu opens beside it.
- Two new views show the Zero Trust plan: the swimlane board and the table.
- Until now the demo showed only the generic pack menu. It now carries the Zero Trust pack's own menu and the plan, using the same sample data as the report's dev server. To make that repeatable I:
  - added `report/scripts/export-demo-data.mjs`, which writes that sample data;
  - extended `website/scripts/build-demo-report.mjs` to embed attachments.

**What's missing: Microsoft's own Zero Trust report**
- The only copy I found is `ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html` in the maester-cloud repo. It comes from the real demo tenant and names real people. Among others: Manoj Kesana, Afif Ahmed, Shonali Balakrishna and Wilna Rossouw.
- The demo build now replaces every name and address it knows about and fails if any is left. Even so, the safety check blocked me from reading that file into the public demo.
- Once the report is added, rerun the capture script. That adds a "Zero Trust report" view to the showcase automatically.

There are two ways to add it:
- **You run the build with that file:** the command is below. The build fails if it finds a known name, but please look over the report before it goes public. People named only in plain text, not in links or addresses, may not be on my list.
- **Use a clean tenant:** generate a fresh Zero Trust Assessment report against a tenant with no real people in it.

```bash
cd website && node scripts/build-demo-report.mjs ../report/dist/index.html /tmp/maester-demo/results.json --attach "zero-trust-workshop=/tmp/maester-demo/zero-trust-workshop.json" --attach "Zero Trust Assessment=$HOME/github/maester-cloud/scripts/local-samples/zt/ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html"
```

The two `/tmp/maester-demo` files come from `report/scripts/export-demo-data.mjs`. Run `cd report && node scripts/export-demo-data.mjs /tmp/maester-demo` first; the report template must already be built (`npm run build` in `report/`).

# AGENTS.md

Maester is a PowerShell framework for monitoring Microsoft 365 security
configuration, with its own test engine. Pester is used only for the module's unit tests
and to run users' Pester-format custom tests. Requires PowerShell 7.4+. Monorepo: `powershell/` (module source),
`tests/` (security checks shipped to users), `src/Maester.Engine/` (C# engine core,
built DLL committed in `powershell/lib/`), `build/`, `website/` (Astro + Starlight,
maester.dev), `report/` (React app that builds the HTML report template).

## Two unrelated test trees — don't mix them

- `tests/` — Maester **security checks** that ship to end-user tenants, run via
  `Invoke-Maester`. Each check is a native test: `tests/<suite>/[<service>/]Test.<ID>.ps1`
  (one function with a `[MaesterTest(...)]` attribute) plus `Test.<ID>.md`. No
  `*.Tests.ps1` wrappers, no connection/licence guards, no outer try/catch: declare
  `Service`/`License` and the engine handles them. Scaffold with `New-MtTest`,
  validate with `Get-MtTest <ID>` (`Get-MtTest -Path` applies the rules of a custom test
  and does not report a missing attribute), run with `Invoke-MtTest -Path`; `Convert-MtTest`
  converts users' Pester-format tests. New MT.xxxx checks go here; follow
  `.github/skills/maester-test-expert/SKILL.md` and `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx`,
  and choose the attribute values with `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md`
  (see "Reviewing a test's attributes" below). A benchmark test for a requirement that another
  suite already checks is a shim that returns that test's result (see "Reviewing a test for
  duplicates" below).
- `powershell/tests/` — **unit tests for the module itself**.

## Commands

- Unit tests: `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` — run before pushing. These enforce
  naming, exports, help, and PSScriptAnalyzer conventions; fix what they flag.
- Build module: `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1`; validate: `./build/Test-MaesterModuleOutput.ps1`
- Website: `cd website && npm ci && npm start` · Report: `cd report && npm ci && npm run build`

## Hard rules

- Generated content — regenerate, never hand-edit: `website/src/data/versions.json`, `website/versioned_docs/` (the frozen 2.x docs), everything under
  `powershell/internal/generated/`, and the native `tests/eidsca/Test.EIDSCA.*` and
  `tests/orca/Test.ORCA.*` files the generators in `build/eidsca/` and `build/orca/`
  write. Edit the PowerShell source, comment-based help or generator templates and let
  automation regenerate. `powershell/assets/MaesterServicePlanNames.json` (Microsoft's friendly name for each
  licence service plan) is written with `website/src/data/license-service-plans.json` by
  `website/scripts/update-license-service-plans.mjs`. `powershell/assets/ConsoleContributors.json` (the dashboard's
  Featured contributor list) is written by `./build/Update-ConsoleContributors.ps1` from
  the website's contributor data.
- Never commit the website data that each build generates: the command pages in `website/docs/commands/`
  (everything but `readme.mdx`), `website/src/data/test-catalog.json`, `contributors.json`, `sponsors.json`,
  `community-packs.json` and `catalog-history.json`. They are ignored by git. `website/scripts/prepare-data.mjs`
  writes them from the module source, the git history, GitHub and packs.maester.cloud before `npm run dev` and
  `npm run build`; `npm run refresh-data` writes them again.
  The build-website workflow builds and deploys maester.dev from main, so a merge needs no follow-up PR.
- A test is mapped to a framework in one place: the `Control` attribute, `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`. A
  CIS test carries `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'`, a CISA test `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'`, and any other
  test may name the same requirements. An ASD test carries `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'` (or `ism:<id>` for a
  control outside the maturity model). Every test in `tests/cis`, `tests/cisa` and `tests/asd` must name a requirement of its
  suite's framework. The engine builds `Benchmark` from the first `Control` that a framework file knows and adds
  that requirement's `Related` references to `Control`; do not repeat those, and do not add benchmark tags.
- A framework file is a catalogue, not a list of tests: `tests/<suite>/frameworks/<key>.json`
  (`tests/cis/frameworks/cis-m365.json`, `tests/cis/frameworks/cis-github.json`,
  `tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json`, and the generated `tests/asd/frameworks/essential-eight.json` and
  `tests/asd/frameworks/ism.json`, written by `build/asd/Update-AsdFramework.ps1` from the ISM OSCAL release),
  declared in the suite's `suite.json` (`Frameworks`: `Key`,
  `Version`). It holds the framework's name and version and each requirement's `Id` and facts (CIS `Level` and
  `Profile`; CISA `Criticality`, `Upstream` and `Related` NIST references; Essential Eight `Level` and `Strategy`;
  ISM `Guideline`, `Section` and `Applicability`), never the text of a benchmark and
  never a `Tests` list. When a new test implements a requirement the file does not have, add the requirement in
  the same commit, or `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1` and the unit tests fail.
- Checks read through the session cache. A run reports on one snapshot of the tenant, so no check, pack or helper
  passes `-DisableCache` or otherwise bypasses the Graph or GitHub cache, even to read data that changed during the
  session. Only the transport helpers listed in `powershell/tests/general/GraphCacheUsage.Tests.ps1` may offer the
  switch, and that test fails on any other use. Don't apply a review suggestion to bypass the cache.

## Repository layout — where files go

Full rules and reasoning: `website/docs/contributing.md` ("Repository layout"), published at
https://maester.dev/docs/contributing#repository-layout. `powershell/tests/general/RepositoryLayout.Tests.ps1`
enforces them. When writing or reviewing a change, check every added, moved or renamed file:

- Folder names under `tests/`, `powershell/` and `build/` are lowercase kebab-case
  (`global-secure-access`, not `GlobalSecureAccess`). No two paths may differ only in case.
- One name per service, the same everywhere: `ad`, `azure`, `azure-devops`, `copilot`,
  `copilot-studio`, `defender`, `entra`, `exchange`, `fabric`, `foundry`, `github`,
  `global-secure-access`, `graph`, `intune`, `purview`, `sharepoint`, `teams`, `xspm`.
  Folders name the product whose settings a check reads, never a theme: an AI check goes in
  the folder of its product (an Entra agent identity check in `entra/`) and declares
  `Area = 'ai'`. A new service must be added to the guide and the test.
- `tests/<suite>/` holds only `Test.<ID>.ps1`, `Test.<ID>.md`, `suite.json` and `README.md`, plus the suite's
  framework files, `frameworks/<key>.json` beside its `suite.json` (lowercase key; nothing else goes in a
  `frameworks/` folder).
  Suites: `maester/<service>/` (plus `drift/`; `maester/xspm/` has its own suite.json),
  `cis/`, `cisa/<service>/`, `asd/<service>/`, `ad/<area>/`, generated `eidsca/` and `orca/`, and `custom/`
  (reserved for users; never commit tests there).
- `powershell/public/` (exported) is grouped by job: `run/`, `connect/`, `report/`, `app/`,
  `packs/`, `services/<service>/`. `powershell/internal/` uses `engine/`, `session/`, `connect/`,
  `report/`, `app/`, `packs/`, `services/<service>/`, `checks/<suite>/<service>/`, `generated/`,
  `utility/`. Nothing sits directly in `public/` or `internal/`.
- `packs/<name>/` at the repository root holds the Maester Packs that ship with Maester (ID `maester.<name>`,
  a code of the pack's own such as `ZTA`, test IDs `<Code>.<n>` without the `MP.` that installed packs use). They are not under `tests/`: a pack loads into its own private
  module, and its rows carry `Source = Custom` and `Package`. See `packs/README.md`.
- Put a function by its job, not by the check that first needed it: reusable data access
  for a service goes in `internal/services/<service>/`; logic only one suite's checks use
  goes in `internal/checks/<suite>/<service>/`; a helper users call from custom tests goes
  in `public/services/<service>/` (and in the manifest's `FunctionsToExport`).
- One function per file, named `Verb-Noun.ps1` after the function, with an approved verb.
- Custom tests can call only exported commands. To make an internal helper available to them,
  `git mv` it from `internal/services/<service>/` to `public/services/<service>/`, add it to
  `FunctionsToExport`, and give it full comment-based help (see "Making an internal helper public"
  in the contributing guide). Exporting a command makes it public API; flag a promotion in review.

## Reviewing a test for duplicates

Benchmarks overlap, and a check that CIS, CISA, ASD and Maester each implement in their own way gives
two answers for one setting and drifts with every benchmark update. When you write, change or review a
test, look for a duplicate before the attribute review:

1. Find the tests in every suite that read the same setting (`Get-MtTest -Product <key> -Feature <key>`,
   and a search of `tests/` for the Graph endpoint or setting name).
2. If one exists, read what the benchmark asks in its own sources, not only the requirement's one-line
   text: its audit or assessment guidance and any reference configuration it publishes (for ASD, the
   ISM, the Essential Eight assessment process guide and the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud). Note
   every concrete value they name, and whether it differs from the existing test.
3. Decide, as "Tests that another suite already has" in `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx` says:
   - the benchmark asks for what the existing test checks: the new test is a shim, a test whose body is
     `return <the existing test's function>`, with its own `Id`, `Title`, `Control` and guide;
   - it asks for the same check with a different value the existing test takes as a parameter: a shim
     that passes the value;
   - it asks for something no test checks, or a rule no parameter covers: a test of its own, which
     reads data through `powershell/internal/services/<service>/` helpers instead of copying another
     test's logic.
4. Fail the review when a benchmark test re-implements a check another suite already has and the
   benchmark's sources give no reason, or when a helper named after a suite (`Get-MtAsd*`,
   `Get-MtCis*`) does data access that is not specific to that suite. Say which test it duplicates
   and which source you read.

`powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1` checks the mechanical part: a shim declares the same
attribute values as the test it calls (`Product` to `Mitre`, `Service`, `License` and the other gates),
calls a test that exists and is not a shim, passes only parameters that test declares, leaves its own
requirement off that test's `Control`, and names that test in its guide. Whether the benchmark asks for
the same thing is the reviewer's judgement.

## Reviewing a test's attributes

Every built-in test declares what it is about, how urgent a failure is and which attack techniques
it addresses: `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `UserImpact`,
`ImplementationCost`, `Mitre` and, where one applies, `RelatedProduct`. The rules for each value
are in `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md` (the rubric); the allowed keys are in
`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`.

When you write, change or review a test, check its attributes against the rubric as a separate
step, after the code review and before you approve or hand off:

1. Read the test's `.ps1` and `.md` and state in one sentence what it checks and what the fix is.
2. For each attribute that is new or changed, decide whether the declared value fits the rubric. A
   value fails only when the rubric clearly gives a different one; say which value and which rule.
3. Fail the review if any value does not fit. Do not approve with a note to fix it later.

Three things enforce this, in order:

- `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1` fails on anything mechanical: a missing
  attribute, a key that is not in the taxonomy, a retired ATT&CK technique, a taxonomy tag on a
  built-in test.
- The `attribute-review` workflow (`.github/workflows/attribute-review.yaml`) runs a reviewer model
  against the rubric on every pull request that adds a test or changes one of these attributes, and
  fails the check with the value it expected and the reason. It calls the Claude API with the
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret; without the secret it reports that the review was skipped. To run
  the same review locally before pushing, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and run
  `./build/review/Invoke-MtAttributeReview.ps1 -BaseRef origin/main -OutputPath ./TestResults`
  (`TestResults/` is ignored by git; without `-OutputPath` the report is written to the current
  folder).
- The person or agent reviewing the pull request applies the same rubric and is the last word. A
  maintainer who disagrees with the workflow can apply the `attribute-review-override` label and
  should say why in the pull request.

## Labelling pull requests, issues and discussions

Labels follow one rubric so the queue can be filtered by status, type and product. The
labels are defined in `.github/labels.json`; the rules for choosing them are in
`.github/skills/maester-triage/SKILL.md`. To triage, use the `maester-triage` agent (or follow
the skill directly): it shows its plan before changing anything and only ever changes labels.
After editing `.github/labels.json`, run `./build/github/Sync-GitHubLabels.ps1` to see the
changes and `-Apply` to make them. `-Apply` creates, renames and updates labels and copies a merged
label onto the items that carry the old one; add `-DeleteMerged` to also delete the old labels.

## Agents and skills

The agents and skills in this repository are listed in `website/docs/agents-and-skills.md`. Each
has one source file: `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` or `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. The
Claude Code copies under `.claude/agents/` and `.claude/skills/`, and that docs page, are generated
from them by `./build/github/Update-AgentFiles.ps1`. Edit the source file, run the script, and
commit both; never edit a generated copy. `powershell/tests/general/AgentFiles.Tests.ps1` fails
when they drift.

- [Contributors attribution system](contributors-attribution-system.md) — registry + git-derived credits for maester.dev
- [Maester 3.0 design](maester-3-design.md) — design doc, owner rulings, status (M0–M9 done on PR 2334, design changes awaiting sign-off)
- [Maester Packs design](maester-marketplace-design.md) — packs/connectors marketplace draft + mockup; owner rulings 2026-10-07, some items open
- [Maester 3.0 console output](maester-3-console-output.md) — TUI/perf rulings 2026-10-10, shipped on PR 2334, open follow-ups; 2026-10-18 boxed main column + pipeline built (uncommitted branch)
- [Test taxonomy research](maester-test-taxonomy-research.md) — framework/MITRE mapping research + clean-slate attribute design; lives in maester-cloud, never in Maester; Category/Tag may change
- [Console easter egg](maester-console-easter-egg.md) — hidden game in the 3.0 dashboard; stealth rule (no docs, no push until asked), trigger `dead`
- [Preview test titles](preview-test-titles.md) — no "(Preview)" in titles; read existing PR reviews before reviewing
- [Skip draft PRs](skip-draft-prs.md) — ignore contributors' draft PRs when triaging; one-line mention at most
- [Benchmark shims](map-benchmarks-to-existing-tests.md) — a benchmark test duplicating another suite's check is a shim; review new tests for duplicates against the benchmark's own sources
- [CIS 4.1 shim PR](cis-4-1-shim-pending.md) — PR 2720 (refactor/cis-m365-4-1-shim), opened in the 3.0 freeze; Step clash with PR 2683 decides merge order
- [PR review on GitHub](pr-review-on-github.md) — PR Desk retired 2026-11-04; review in chat, post to GitHub; assignee, last-push and CIS rulings
- [maester.dev redesign](maester-dev-site-redesign.md) — Astro+Starlight rebuild on feat/website-astro worktree (2026-11-02), preview-default docs, URL contract, HyperFrames
- [Report redesign](maester-3-report-redesign.md) — 3.0 HTML report redesign, PR 2646 (2026-11-03), data additions, icon terms
- [SCuBA packs in own repos](scuba-packs-own-repos.md) — ScubaGear/ScubaGoggles packs: one maester365 repo per pack, not Maester's packs/; ScubaGear published at maester365/maester-pack-scubagear (no release yet)
- [Report intelligence plan](maester-report-intelligence.md) — defender's path: design doc on feat/defenders-path (PR 2683), measures not tests, all seven milestones on PR 2683 (2026-11-06), untested on a tenant
- [Catalog growth showcase](catalog-growth-showcase.md) — count every test (no toggle), smooth growth chart, community packs in the catalog, badged and listed last
- [PR rulings 2026-11-08](pr-rulings-2026-11-08.md) — taxonomy keys for #2540, bot workflow #2637, MT.1253/1266 stay tests, CIS parked-domain scope
